meta.summary: Phase-by-phase re-research of all four Permian Express rows. Changes: PE1 capacity 200k->150k bpd (200k is PE2's figure); PE2 StartLocation Wichita Falls->Midland (PE2 originates Midland/Garden City/Colorado City; Wichita Falls is PE1's origin); PE4 length 400mi->0 and diameter 24in->blank (PE4 was an expansion of existing pipe, no new mainline; EIA's 400mi = 'length of pipeline affected'); parent split 88/12->87.7/12.3 (both partners' FY2025 10-Ks); Operator fill = Sunoco Pipeline L.P. (TX RRC P-5 ID 829627); EndLocation fills (Nederland); OtherEnglishNames cleanup. PE3 row fully confirmed as-is.

Parent.old: Energy Transfer LP [88.00%]; Exxon Mobil Corp [12.00%]
Parent.new: Energy Transfer LP [87.70%]; Exxon Mobil Corp [12.30%]
Parent.evidence: ET FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-19) asset table: 'Permian Express Pipelines | 87.7%'; XOM FY2025 10-K Ex-21 (filed 2026-02-18): 'Permian Express Partners LLC (5) 12.3 Delaware'. Two independent filers, sum exactly 100. Same 87.7% in ET FY2024 10-K.

Operator.evidence: TX RRC tariff TX No. 5.11.0 (eff. 2024-07-01): 'Operated under Permian Express Partners LLC's T-4 Permit No 09001 and Sunoco Pipeline L.P.'s P5 ID 829627'; SXL FY2016 10-K: 'We maintain a controlling financial and voting interest in PEP and are the operator of all of the assets'. Sunoco Pipeline L.P. is a wholly owned ET subsidiary per ET FY2025 10-K glossary.

Owner [ref].evidence: Owner1 = Permian Express Partners LLC [100%] CONFIRMED: ET FY2025 10-K ('PEP — Permian Express Partners LLC, a non-wholly owned subsidiary of Energy Transfer' + lists PE 1/2/3/4 in the JV); XOM Ex-21 still lists PEP holding. No divestiture found 2021-2026.

Capacity.evidence: SXL Q3 2012 8-K: 'initial capacity of 90,000 barrels per day, with full capacity of 150,000 barrels per day on-line in late 2013 or early 2014'; NASM 2017 retrospective: 'entered service in 2013, transporting 150,000 barrels per day of crude from Wichita Falls, Texas, to Nederland'; EIA Liquids Pipeline Projects DB: PE1 new-build +90k (2013 Q2) + PE1 expansion +60k (2014 Q1) = 150k, note 'Capacity increased from 90,000 b/d to 150,000 b/d'. The 200,000 bpd figure belongs to PE2 (SXL Q4 2013 8-K, SXL FY2013 10-K, Alon USA Partners 10-K all attach ~200k to Permian Express 2).

OtherEnglishNames.evidence: PE1 and PE2 are separate GEM rows (P0113 / P2581); listing both names on both rows conflates them (likely the source of the capacity mix-up).

EndLocation.evidence: OGJ 2012-06-27: 'continuous pipeline service from Wichita Falls, Tex., to Nederland and Beaumont, Tex.'; Hart Energy 2012-10-01: 'combined service from Wichita Falls to Beaumont' (also serves Beaumont; Nederland terminal is the primary delivery point per ET filings).

StartLocation [ref].evidence: Wichita Falls origin CONFIRMED by OGJ + Hart Energy (independent).

confirmations.StartYear1: 2013 — SXL Q2 2013 8-K ('commenced operations as scheduled in the second quarter'); GlobalData 'operational since 2013'. Full 150k capacity reached late 2013/early 2014. High.
confirmations.StartLocation: Wichita Falls — OGJ + Hart Energy. High.
confirmations.FuelSource: Permian Basin — Hart Energy (receives from Basin Pipeline interconnect carrying Permian crude); ET FY2025 10-K. High.

flags.LengthKnown: 300 mi UNVERIFIED — no non-GEM source states 300 mi for PE1. Only published figure is GlobalData 611 km (~380 mi, single source); GEM's own route-derived LengthEstimateKm is 641 km, much closer to GlobalData than to 483 km (300 mi). PE1 = reversed Wichita Falls-Wortham line + excess capacity on West Texas Gulf southern leg, so length depends on segments counted. Recommend review; not changed (no 2-source figure).
flags.Diameter: Left blank — GlobalData says max 16 in (single source, low tier); no operator filing gives PE1 diameter. Do not confuse with Sunoco's 14-in Wichita Falls Crude Pipeline (different line).

StartLocation.evidence: SXL FY2015 10-K: 'origins in multiple locations in Western Texas: Midland, Garden City and Colorado City'; EIA DB: new-build segments Garden City->Colorado City (20") and Colorado City->Corsicana (24"). Wichita Falls appears in NO PE2 description in any SXL/ET filing FY2013-FY2025 — it is PE1's origin. Midland origin connects via the SunVit lateral (consolidated into Sunoco Nov 2016, per OGJ 2016-11-10).

EndLocation.evidence: SXL Q3 2013 8-K: 'takeaway capacity from the rapidly developing Permian Basin region to multiple markets on the Gulf Coast, including our Nederland terminal'; RBN project page: 'Destination: Nederland, TX'. Note: PE2 new-build mainline ends at Corsicana; barrels reach Nederland over the existing Sunoco/ET system.

confirmations.Status: operating — ET FY2025 10-K; RBN 'Operational'; GlobalData 'operational since 2015'. High.
confirmations.StartYear1: 2015 — SXL Q2 2015 8-K ('Commenced operations ... in July 2015'); EIA 2015 Q3; RBN Q3/2015. High.
confirmations.Capacity: 230,000 bpd — EIA DB 230,000 b/d; RBN 'Base Capacity: 230 Mb/d'. Operator's announced figure was 'approximately 200,000 bpd' at 2015 startup; 230k is the post-startup nameplate carried by both independent compilers. Initial-capacity nuance noted in ResearcherNotes.
confirmations.LengthKnown: 334 mi — EIA DB 334 mi; GlobalData 537 km (=334 mi). (RBN says 400 mi, likely counting connected laterals/existing pipe.) High.
confirmations.Diameter: 20, 24 in — EIA DB with segment attribution (Garden City-Colorado City 20", Colorado City-Corsicana 24"); GlobalData 'maximum diameter of 24 inches'. 20-in leg single-source (EIA) but segment-explicit. High.

OtherEnglishNames.evidence: Naming consistency with sibling rows; PE3 is the universal name in filings/press.

confirmations.Status: operating — ET FY2018 10-K 'fully operational in September 2018'; ET FY2025 10-K current asset list; EIA 'Completed'. High.
confirmations.StartYear1: 2017 — ET Q3 2018 8-K (in service Q4 2017); EIA partial 100k b/d Q4 2017, final 40k Q3 2018. High.
confirmations.Capacity: 140,000 bpd — ETP Business Wire May 2018 ('140,000 barrels per day Phase 1 of Permian Express 3', archived); Tom Long Aug 2018 call (SEC Form 425); EIA 140,000 b/d. High.
confirmations.LengthKnown: 0 (expansion treatment) CONFIRMED — ET Aug 2018 investor deck (SEC Form 425): PE3 provides takeaway 'utilizing existing pipelines'; EIA PE3 row has blank mileage AND blank diameter while sibling new-build rows carry pipe specs. No source anywhere assigns PE3 a length or diameter. (EIA labels project type 'New' = new service/capacity, not new pipe.) Medium-high (one explicit primary statement + consistent independent indirect evidence).

flags.start_detail: Final-tranche timing discrepancy for notes: EIA says final 40k online Q3 2018 and ET FY2018 10-K says 'fully operational in September 2018' (=Q3), but ET's Q4 2018 earnings release books 'the expansion of our Permian Express 3 pipeline in service in the fourth quarter of 2018'. StartYear1=2017 unaffected.

LengthKnown.evidence: PE4 was an EXPANSION of the existing PE system, not new pipe -> tracker convention LengthKnown=0. ET investor deck Sept 2018 (SEC Form 425): 'Permian Express 4 Expansion Project (formerly PE3 Phase II)'; ET COO McCrea Q2 2018 call (SEC Form 425), answering a question about squeezing capacity from existing Permian pipes with drag-reducing agents: 'we are looking at expanding Perm Express 3, which would be Permian Express 4'; every ET quarterly release calls it 'the Permian Express 4 expansion'; EIA project type 'Expansion' and EIA's Definitions sheet states that for pump-station expansions 'length of pipeline affected is shown' — so EIA's 400 mi (the evident origin of GEM's value) is affected-mainline length, not new pipe. RBN lists 334 mi (= the existing PE2 mainline), and the 334-vs-400 disagreement between compilers is itself a tell. No source describes new mainline construction, looping mileage, or a construction contract.

LengthKnownUnits.evidence: Match Phase III expansion-row convention (0 km).

Diameter.evidence: Expansion with no new pipe -> Diameter blank per convention. The 24-in (EIA/RBN) is the diameter of the EXISTING affected mainline (EIA's PE2 note: 'Colorado City to Corsicana, Texas, has 24-inch diameter pipeline').

StartLocation.evidence: ET CFO Tom Long, Q3 2019 earnings call: PE4 'added an additional 120,000 barrels per day of capacity to our Permian Express pipeline system from Colorado City to Nederland, Texas'. (RBN gives Midland as system receipt origin; company statement specifies the expanded corridor starts at Colorado City.) Single explicit source for the corridor start -> medium.
StartLocation.alternative: Keep 'Permian' as system origin if corridor-start framing is not wanted.

EndLocation.evidence: ET CFO quote above; RBN project page: 'Destination: Energy Transfer Nederland Terminal, TX'.

FuelSource.evidence: ET Q2 2019 8-K: 'adds 120,000 barrels per day of capacity from the Permian Basin to Gulf Coast markets'; RBN project page. (Sibling rows carry FuelSource=Permian Basin; this row was blank.)
